newsitem.title: USA: Goldman offers to drop claim if Simpson confesses.
newsitem.headline: Goldman offers to drop claim if Simpson confesses.

text.p: The father of Ronald Goldman offered on Wednesday to ignore the multimillion-dollar judgment he won against O.J. Simpson for the death of his son if the former football star confesses to murder.

A jury in Simpson's wrongful death civil trial last week blamed him for the June 12, 1994, murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend Ronald Goldman. It awarded Fred Goldman, his father, and Sharon Rufo, his mother, $8.5 million in compensatory damages for the loss of their son's love and support.

On Monday the same jury added $12.5 million in punitive damages to Goldman and his ex-wife and another $12.5 million in punitive damages to Nicole Brown Simpson's estate. Simpson was found innocent of the killings in a 1995 criminal trial.
Fred Goldman said in an interview on Wednesday with KCBS television in Los Angeles that he did not want the money, he wanted Simpson to confess to the murders.

"If the person whose name I don't use that murdered my son wants to write out a complete confession and publish it in newspapers around the country, we'll be glad to ignore the judgment," Goldman said.
